category_summary_html:
🌟 Hermes Ecosystem Newsletter: Top Updates for Hermes Users

💡 Feature Releases & Infrastructure

* Advanced Delegation Modes Plugin: @NousResearch and top author @Teknium have announced the Advanced Delegation plugin. This is a massive update that allows the Hermes Agent orchestrator to pick different models or profiles for subagent tasks, offering highly configurable routing.

* Cloud Availability: @Teknium confirmed that new Hermes Agent subscriptions are going live, meaning subscribers will automatically get an instance on the cloud.

* API Development: Significant progress is being made on the unified gateway API pull request, indicating continued backend enhancement for the platform.

🚀 Community Projects & Performance

* Oh My Hermes (OMH) Ecosystem: rlaope is pushing significant hardware benchmarks for oh-my-hermes as an operating layer for the Hermes Agent.

* Community Engagement: @NousResearch is building strong community ties, hosting an anti-slop hackathon in NYC at Pangram HQ and offering positive feedback to user-created agents.

🔮 Roadmap & Insights

* Upcoming Launches: @NousResearch teased upcoming releases on Friday, signaling a busy release cycle. @Teknium also confirmed a major feature is launching 'literally tomorrow.'

* Honest Roadmap Status: In a transparent update, @Teknium provided a candid assessment of a feature's current outlook, noting that the proactive-agent functionality is still being evaluated, while also admitting challenges like leadership changes for the Hermes Desktop effort.

items.title: @real_kukuruza Neither, exactly. A failed node isn't rerun as-is. dag-ulw adds a repair group for it...
items.content: @real_kukuruza Neither, exactly. A failed node isn't rerun as-is. dag-ulw adds a repair group for it (max 2 cycles per node). Once that group is accepted, the failed node counts as repaired. Its downstream nodes were held all along, so they run for the first time and read the repair group's handoff instead of the failed node's. The exception is a verification node, which reruns itself after its repair. Already-accepted nodes are never rerun automatically. If one needs redoing, it has to be added to the repair group.

items.summary: rlaope gives a detailed technical explanation of how dag-ulw handles failed nodes: repair groups with max two cycles per node, downstream nodes reading the repair group handoff, verification nodes rerunning themselves, and accepted nodes never auto-rerun.

Traffic outgrew our GPUs last week, so we added more B300 ...
items.content:
Meet DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Ultrafast.

Traffic outgrew our GPUs last week, so we added more B300 nodes.

https://t.co/YPSUt2MLNg

Serving capacity is now 3x what it was.

We also doubled the per-key concurrency limit (8 → 16), so you should hit far fewer 429s when you run requests in parallel.

@OpenGatewayai Same model ID. Nothing to change on your side.

web: https://t.co/BBvtMgSSEE

#deepseek #ultrafast #model
